subject: Neptune Labs — renewal scope, bakeoff request and capacity ask
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@neptunelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Neptune Labs Procurement <procurement@neptunelabs.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Neptune Labs renewal window — Q3 bakeoff?

Karthik,

We’re approaching our renewal (July 31) and procurement has flagged a potential bakeoff: OrionAI is pushing for a replacement on throughput/cost. Before procurement opens a full RFP, the execs asked for a short bakeoff plan and cost/latency comparisons so they can decide whether to proceed.

High level asks from my side:
- A throughput baseline on our current workload (avg token/sec per model + tails)
- A short-run bakeoff plan we can run in our environment (preferred) or with a Redwood-managed sandbox
- Any capacity uplift options and pricing for +30% and +100% sustained traffic
- Proposed commercial path if we need to move from hosted to a dedicated pool (SLA/lead times)

We can share a sample query set and logs. Can you propose a timeline? Procurement also wants to know if Redwood can commit to a short-term holdback price for renewal if we start the bakeoff.

Thanks — Asha
Asha Rao
CPO, Neptune Labs
asha@neptunelabs.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <asha@neptunelabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neptune Labs renewal window — Q3 bakeoff?

Asha — thanks for the clear ask. We absolutely want to keep Neptune on Redwood and avoid a protracted RFP. Proposed next steps: 

1) Quick baseline: we’ll run a short profiling pass on a 48-hour sample against your query set to capture latency percentiles, KV/cache hit behavior, and token/sec. Deliverable: snapshot CSV and a 2-page heatmap. (We’ll need the sample logs you mentioned.)

2) Bakeoff plan: 5-day technical bakeoff with two tracks — Redwood-hosted sandbox (fastest) and an on-prem connector POC if you prefer local network parity. We’ll include: identical model versions, identical tokenization, and a fixed traffic replay driver.

3) Capacity options: outline for +30% and +100% sustained: for +30% we recommend a burst-enabled dedicated pool, for +100% we recommend a dedicated cluster with pre-warm (lead time ~3–4 weeks) and short SLA add-on. I’ll surface estimated list/committed pricing in the offer doc.

4) Commercial guardrail: we can hold current renewal effective price for 30 days while the bakeoff runs, provided the statement of work (SOW) is signed to cover the trial infra. We can escalate an executive-to-executive hold if procurement requires longer.

Attachments: draft_redwood_bakeoff_plan.pdf (high level) and a small script we use to sample traffic.

Can Laura and Priyom join a quick call tomorrow morning for technical scoping?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <asha@neptunelabs.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neptune Labs renewal window — Q3 bakeoff?

On 2028-05-30 16:10, karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Asha — thanks for the clear ask. We absolutely want to keep Neptune on Redwood and avoid a protracted RFP. Proposed next steps: 

Hi Asha — quick technical notes so procurement has visibility:
- We’ll need a representative 48-hour traffic export (JSONL) including full prompts and timestamps and an example model artifact (model name + config).
- For the hosted sandbox we’ll mirror your production seed traffic at 1:1 using our replay driver; typical turnaround 48–72 hours to get meaningful percentiles.
- For an on-prem connector POC we use our VPC agent (lightweight) and collect KV+memory profiles; expect a 1 week lead to provision access and security review.

I’m attaching our bakeoff checklist and a short opmetrics export from a similar retail customer so you can see format: neptune_q1_throughput_snapshot.csv, opmetrics-benchmark-notes.txt.

Two caveats: 
- If you need very long context (>8k tokens) for the majority of queries we’ll need to map kernel selection to maintain latency SLOs; that can influence the recommended dedicated sizing.
- For the +100% sustained scenario we typically recommend a quantized model variant to reduce cost per token. We can run a quick side-by-side on quantized vs fp16 in the bakeoff.

Available for a scoping call 10:00–11:30 PT tomorrow.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Rao <asha@neptunelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Neptune Labs Procurement <procurement@neptunelabs.com>
Date: 2028-05-31T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neptune Labs renewal window — Q3 bakeoff?

Thanks — that timeline looks workable. A couple of points from my side: 
- Procurement wants a pricing comparison table vs OrionAI (they’ve already shared a draft pricing sheet). Can Redwood do a matched-config price estimate for host vs dedicated for +30% and +100%?
- We’d prefer the on-prem connector for the bakeoff to ensure network parity; security will need to run through the VPC agent checklist — I’ll loop in our security folks after the call.
- If OrionAI is already in procurement, I need an executive note outlining: why Redwood is the lower operational risk, and what we would commit to (timeline + capacity + temporary holdback).

Can you include an exec summary in the offer and a one-page SLA comparison? Also — what’s the typical lead time to stand up a dedicated pool if we sign for +30%?

If we can surface a POC SOW and a short-term price hold, procurement will likely defer a full RFP and keep this a bakeoff.

— Asha
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <asha@neptunelabs.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-01T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Neptune Labs renewal window — Q3 bakeoff?

Asha — looping in commercial options and escalation path.

We can deliver: 
- A matched-configuration pricing worksheet for host vs dedicated for both +30% and +100% (attached).
- Exec summary one-pager and an SLA comparison to OrionAI (we’ll call out network parity, KV-caching, and our rollback/fallback behavior).
- For +30% sustained we can provision a burst-enabled dedicated pool within ~10 business days from SOW sign; for a fully pre-warmed dedicated cluster for +100% expect ~3 weeks.

As a commercial gesture to avoid a lengthy RFP, Redwood can offer a 90-day price hold on existing renewal pricing if Neptune signs a POC SOW to run the bakeoff within the next 21 days. I’ve drafted a quick DocuSign path here: https://www.docusign.com/NEP-2028-045/offer — we can tighten terms on the SOW to cover infra and security review.

I’ll prepare the matched pricing and the one-pager and drop into HubSpot (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NEP-2028-045) by end of day tomorrow.

If procurement needs an exec touch, I’m happy to join a call with your CPO or Head of Infrastructure.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf, neptune_q1_throughput_snapshot.csv, opmetrics-benchmark-notes.txt
